document_summary: City of Boston FAQ for tenants on the Housing Stability Notification Act (HSNA), a notice-of-rights ordinance requiring landlords to give tenants a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources with a notice to quit or non-renewal.

rules.title: [notice-only] Boston Housing Stability Notification Act
rules.requirement: A landlord or foreclosing owner ending a tenancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to Quit or notice of lease non-renewal. A copy of the notice, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, must also be sent to the City's Office of Housing Stability.
rules.key_value: Notice-of-rights requirement only; no just-cause protection
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords/foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston.
rules.exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; and in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse.
rules.interaction: Notice-only ordinance; does not limit the grounds for eviction or non-renewal under state law. A violation does not halt the eviction process.
rules.citation: Boston Municipal Code § 10-11.7 (Housing Stability Notification Act)
rules.quoted_span:
The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord
decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement.
rules.conflict_note: Notice-of-rights ordinance only; it does not restrict the grounds for eviction or non-renewal, so it is not a just-cause protection.
rules.extraction_notes: Effective date from 'The HSNA becomes effective on November 6, 2020.' The ordinance was passed in October 2020 (exact day not stated). Enforcement: warning for 1st offense, then $300 per day. Source is a city FAQ summarizing the ordinance.
